ticket.title: outfeed plan: -d is the suite dir and the clean check reports an unnamed dirty file at the wrong root
ticket.description:
Two traps found while planning the GB-361/GB-362 release, both costing a wrong first answer.

(1) `outfeed plan -d miter` does not plan miter. -d is the SUITE directory, exactly as it already is for `outfeed install` (which I hit earlier the same way), and the repository is the positional argument. The wrong form fails with `Manifest error in ./Cargo.toml: No such file or directory`, which reads as a broken checkout rather than as a misuse of the flag. The correct form is `outfeed plan miter -d /path/to/suite`.

(2) The clean-working-tree check runs at the harness root, not at the repository being released. With one unrelated modified file in the suite root (an editor rewriting gaugeblock.code-workspace), every member plan refuses with "working tree has uncommitted changes" while `git -C miter status --porcelain` is empty. Reproduced by restoring that file: plans then run. Whether the harness should gate a member release is a question, but the failure told me nothing about where to look - the error names neither the directory checked nor the file at fault.

Wanted: -d documented as the suite directory in `plan --help` (or renamed), and the dirty-tree error naming the repository it actually inspected plus one offending path. Cheap, and both would have saved the twenty minutes this took.
